Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public. 


Mazdoor  Kisan  Shakti  Sangathan 
"The  Right  to  Information,  The  Right  to  Live''

Indian  Standard 

SPECIFICATION    FOR 
METAL  MARKING  PUNCHES 

(  First  Revision  } 


(  Reaffirmed  2006 ) 


1.  Scope  "  Lays  down  the  requirements  for  metal  marking  punches.

2.1  Tolerances — Tolerances  on  untoleranced  dimensions  shall  be  according  to  the  best  prevalent 
manufacturing  practices. 

3.  Specimen  Letters  and  Numerals 

3.1  Capital  Letters 


ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ    « 


I^i^  Note  —  The  punch  for  letter  T  to  be  used  for  marking  dash  lines,  when  used  horizontally, 

3.2  Small  Letters 


^       abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz 

3.3  Hindu-Arabic  Numerals 

0123A5678 


Note  —  The  punch  for  numeral  '6'  to  be  used  for  marking  numeral  '9'  also. 

3.4  Roman  Numerals  and  Arrows 

g|    iniiiivvviviiviiiixx  _► 

4.  Material  —  Suitable  steels  meeting  with  the  requirements  laid  down  in  5  and  8. 

Example-. 

T9  OMn  2W  50  Cr  45  of  Schedule  VI  of  IS  :  1570-1961  'Schedules  for  wrought  steels 
for  general  engineering  purposes' with  a  maximum  sulphur  and  phosphorus  content  of 
0'05  percent  each. 

5.  Hardness  —  The   hardness   of  the  letter  end  shall  be  615  to  700  WV  ( JS  56  to  B2  HRC ).    The 
hardness  of  the  punch  on  striking>nd  shall  be  370  to,485  HV  {^ZB  to  46  HRC  ). 

6.  Designation  —  The  metal   marking  punch^^shall   be  designated  by  the  commonly  used  name,  the 
letter  or  numeral  size  and  the  number  of  this  standard;  / 

Example  1 

A  metal  marking  punch  of  capital  letter  'A'  and  of  size  5  mm  shall  be  designated  as: 

Marking  Punch  Capital  A  —  5    IS  :  6864 

Example  2 

A  metal  marking  punch  set  or  capital  letter  of  size  5  mm  shall  be  designated  as  : 

Marking  Punch  Set  Capital  —  5    IS  :  6864 

Example  3 

A  metal  marking  punch  of  Hindu-Arabic  numeral  3  and  of  10  mm  size  shall  be  designated 
as: 

Marking  Punch  HA  3  —  10     IS  :  6864     ' 

Example  4 

A  metal  marking  punch  set  of  Roman  numerals  and  of  20  mm  size  shall  be  designated  as: 

Marking  Punch  Set  Roman  —  20    IS  :  6864 


IS  :  6864  -  1984 

7.  Application 

7.1  The  punches  shall  normally  be  employed  for  metals  having  a  tensile  strength  up  to  1  200  N/mm* 
(  «  120  kgf/mm^ ).  Punches  for  marking  metals  with  tensile  strength  up  to  1  600  N/mm^  ( '^  160  kgf/ 
mm^ )  are  special  tools  and  they  may,  however,  be  ordered  according  to  this  standard,  in  such  case 
the  punches  shall  be  designated  as  'hard'  (  H  )  as  follows: 

Marking  Punch  Set  Capital  —  HIS:  6864 

Note  —  Steels   of  tensile  strength  1  200  N/mm2  and  1  600  N/mm^   have  approximate  hardness    value  of  370  HV  and 
500  HV ,  respectively. 

8.  Test  —  The  metal  marking  punches  shall  be  tested  on  machined  block  of  steel  having  a  hardness 
of  350  to  450  HV  by  striking  three  blows  from  a  distance  of  500  mm  of  500  g  hammer  conforming 
to  IS  :  841-1983  'Steel  hammer'  on  the  punch  striking  end.  On  the  completion  of  test  the  punches 
shall  not  show  any  sign  of  damage,  distortion  or  chipping  on  either  of  the  ends. 

9.  Packing  —  The  metal  marking  punches  shall  be  supplied  in  sets  and  shall  be  supplied  in  suitable 
steel  cases.    The  packing  shall  be  in  accordance  with  the  best  prevalent  trade  practice, 

10.  Marlcing  —  The'container  of  the  punches  shall  be  marked  with  the  nominal  size  in  millimetres, 
manufacturer's  name  initials  or  recognised  trade-mark  and  the  description  of  the  contents.  The 
appropriate  letter  or  numeral  as  the  case  may  be  shall  be  engraved  on  one  side  of  the  punch  so  as  to 
facilitate  the  correct  holding  of  punch  while  punching.  (  See  Fig.  below.  ) 


Note  —  The  punch  for  numeral '6'   shall   be  marked   on   one  side  with    '6' and  on  the  other  side  with '9*  for  proper 
orientation. 

10.1  ISI  Certification  iVIarl^ing  —  Details  avaMable  with  the  Indian  Standards  Institution. 

11,  Sampling  —  Unless  otherwise  agreed  to  between  the  buyer  and  the  seller  the  procedure  given 
in  IS  :  2500  (Part  1)-1973  'Sampling  inspection  tables:Part  1  Inspection  by  attributes  and  by  count 
of  defects  (  first  revision  )'  may  be  followed  for  sampling  inspection.  The  sampling  plans  for  various 
characteristics  shall  be  according  to  11.1  and  11.2. 

11.1  For  dimensions,  specimen  of  numerals  and  manufacture,  workmanship  and  finish,  single 
sampling  plan  with  inspection  level  III  and  acceptable  quality  level  (  AQL)  of  2'5  percent  [see 
Tables  1  and  3  of  IS  :  2500  (  Part  1  )-1973  ]  shall  be  adopted. 

11.2  For  hardness  and  performance  tests,  single  sampling  plan  \A/ith  inspection  level  I  and  acceptable 
xiuality  level  (AQL)  of  10  percent  [  see  Tables  1  and  2  of  IS  :  2500  (Part  1)-1973  ]  shall  be 
adopted. 


EXPLAN ATOR  Y    N  OTE 

This  specification  was  first  issued  in  1973.  The  current  revision  has  been  taken  up  in  order  to 
include  tire  commonly  used  symbols.  It  is  also  in  alignment  with  the  latest  version  of  DIN 
7353-1978  'Metal  marking  punches'  issued  by  the  Deutsches  Institute  fur  Normung  (  DIN  ).
